name: Tristram's Bunting
rangeDescription: Siberia to northeastern china; winters to southern china and northern thailand
description: Small and distinctive bunting, usually seen moving around quietly in thick undergrowth. Warm rusty brown with a black-and-white striped head.

name: Short-crested Coquette
rangeDescription: Southern mexico (sierra madre del sur of guerrero)
description: Tiny, scarce, and very local hummingbird restricted to humid forest and shade-coffee plantations in foothills of Sierra Madre del Sur, Guerrero. Feeds quietly at middle to high levels in flowering trees.
imageCreditName: Ernesto P. Montes - Birding Mexico Tours

name: Sharp-tailed Ibis
rangeDescription: Llanos of eastern colombia to the guianas and western amazonian brazil
description: A medium-sized wading bird, mostly black with a red bill and legs. Relatively long tail projection imparts a long-bodied appearance which is enhanced by its short legs.

name: Green-naped Tanager
rangeDescription: Highlands of far eastern panama (darién) and adjacent colombia
description: This small tanager has a very limited range near the border of Panama and Colombia. Note the mostly black head with pale greenish spots on the cheek and nape, extensive dark spotting on breast and flanks, rich buffy belly, black back, and blue edges on wing feathers.

name: Black-capped Tanager
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern colombia to northern venezuela and northern ecuador
description: Small, active tanager with notably different male and female plumages. Male is steely blue overall with slightly darker wings.

name: Red-crested Cotinga
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia to western venezuela and western bolivia
description: This plump gray bird is a regular sight atop patches of trees from the temperate forest zone to above treeline in the Andes from Venezuela to Bolivia. The plumage is unremarkable at first glance: both sexes are medium gray with a darker face, blackish wings, and a white band on the tail (visible in flight).

name: Orange-fronted Barbet
rangeDescription: Far southwestern colombia (southeastern nariño) and western ecuador (south to el oro)
description: Chunky black and white bird with a stout bill. Ranges in lowland and foothill rainforest west of the Andes in Ecuador and far southwestern Colombia.

name: Banggai Golden-Bulbul
rangeDescription: Peleng, banggai, and labobo, in banggai islands (off eastern sulawesi)
description: A noticeably long-billed thrush-sized bird with an olive head and upperside and uniform yellow underparts. Pairs or small groups inhabit forests, edges, and plantations in the lowlands and foothills.

name: Norfolk Robin
rangeDescription: Norfolk island
description: Learn about Norfolk Robin: explore photos, sounds, and observations collected by birders around the world.

name: Zenker's Honeyguide
rangeDescription: Southern cameroon and gabon to central african republic, northeastern democratic republic of the congo, and southwestern uganda
description: An infrequently encountered honeyguide of forests and forest edge. Overall olive-green to green in coloration, with upperparts darker than underparts and the brightest green in the wings.

name: Kai Besar White-eye
rangeDescription: Kai besar (kai islands)
description: A small green songbird with a bold white eye-ring and a primarily white underside, except for a yellow throat and base to undertail. Usually found in pairs or singly, roaming through forest, woods, and gardens in lowlands and lower hills.

name: Lompobattang Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Southwestern sulawesi (lompobattang massif)
description: A tiny brown flycatcher with an orange throat, a conspicuous orange mark between bill and eyes, a chestnut tail, and a white belly. Inhabits dense understory of montane forest within its small range in southwest Sulawesi.

name: Marsh Warbler
rangeDescription: Europe to central russia; winters to coastal southeastern africa (kwazulu-natal)
description: Medium-sized brown warbler, very similar to Eurasian Reed-Warbler. Best differentiated by the song, which is delightful, distinctive, loud, and full of mimicry of European and African birds.

name: Green Indigobird
rangeDescription: Locally in zambia, southwestern tanzania, malawi, and zimbabwe
description: Nest parasite that lays its eggs in the nests of Peters’s Twinspot. Breeding males are glossy greenish-black, and in good light may show a paler gray wash across the head and breast.

name: Ashy-headed Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia to ecuador and southern peru (puno)
description: Small, short-billed flycatcher found in the Andes from Venezuela to Peru. Bright yellow below with two pale wingbars.

name: Victorin's Warbler
rangeDescription: Southwestern south africa (western cape and southern eastern cape)
description: A skulky brownish warbler with a ragged tail, warm cinnamon-buff underparts, and a distinctive gray face with a pale yellow eye. It is restricted to damp fynbos, especially boggy areas with sedges and Berzelia, and fern-filled glades along forest edges, where it creeps about mouse-like and is almost always first detected by its characteristic song.

name: Bare-throated Bellbird
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (alagoas) to eastern paraguay and northeastern argentina (misiones)
description: Males are unmistakable snow-white cotingas with a greeny-blue bare face and throat. Females are olive-green above with a streaked belly and gray-brown head.

name: Taiwan Blue-Magpie
rangeDescription: Montane forest of taiwan
description: Large, long-tailed bird with rich blue plumage, black head, coral-red bill and feet, and yellow eye. Inhabits lower foothills to lower montane forests and edges (to 1200 m), occasionally venturing into forested parks.

name: Mongolian Finch
rangeDescription: Sparse montane vegetation of southwestern and central asia
description: A pale, large-billed finch found in dry areas with sparse plant cover. Usually seen in small and medium-sized groups.

name: Chestnut-throated Huet-huet
rangeDescription: Central chile (colchagua to río biobío) and adjacent northwestern neuquén (west-central argentina)
description: Fairly common but elusive; heard far more often than seen. Favors native temperate forest and adjacent shrubbery, especially bamboo.
